correctness.rationale: The explicit four residue classes n=4r+c (c=4,5,6,7) yield centers u_c0110v_c and u_c1001v_c. A shared one-deletion output would require a one-symbol shift across all four differing positions, impossible because 0110 has consecutive 11, so deletion sets are disjoint. For the mixed edit balls, the six-bit nondeterministic scanner recognizes zero-operation, substitution and a single adjacent shift; determinized pair scanner has exactly 64 states. A direct independently implemented output-set enumerator checked deletion separation and overlap floor(n²/4)+4 for n=4..22. Separately independently reconstructed compiled C++ matrix DP checked all 4099 terms in each residue class (CERTIFICATE_OK c=4,5,6,7). With X_r=P^r K_c R_c^r in dimension 64×64, Cayley–Hamilton gives a scalar recurrence of order <=4096; adding the cubic annihilator of a quadratic target gives order <=4099. Exact integer first-4099-term equality therefore proves the claimed overlap for all n>=4, not extrapolation from small cases. The 64-bit bound follows from bounded one-edit scripts from any finite-state boundary state; the verification passed without overflow evidence.
residual_risks: Cayley-Hamilton order 4099 relies on exact pair-automaton state model accepting precisely distinct words; the source C++ and independent checks support this equivalence.
Proof concerns only exhibited family and number of distinct traces, not a global intersection maximum.

originality.rationale: Sala et al. Section V-B indeed defines exactly the composed I_t(D_t) channel and gives alternating-center distance-one, uncoded lower bounds, so that direct same-model prior is explicitly credited. Here the centers have no common one-deletion shadow (distance two in fixed-length Levenshtein), and a new exact quadratic overlap holds for all n. Their Section V-B does not analyze this deletion-correcting pair in inspected full text; single edit alternatives, individual fixed-length balls, and cross insertion-vs-deletion balls are different channel models.
residual_risks: A broader intersection theorem under fixed-length Levenshtein metrics or unindexed combinatorial lemma may cover this particular family.

checked_sources: Sala et al. Section V-B motivated adversarial reconstruction question
Exact constructive all-n pair and deletion-separation proof
value.rationale: The distinct-trace budget under composed deletion/insertion corruption is a natural adversarial reconstruction invariant. A deletion-correcting two-codeword constraint fundamentally removes the easier alternating distance-one witness. An explicit all-length quadratic overlap and exact recurrence certificate supply a nontrivial lower bound even under that structural code condition, and are potentially relevant to trace-count limits. This is an existence bound, not claimed to be extremal.
residual_risks: Lower bound only; no optimality among all pairs or asymptotic coding-rate theorem.

limitations: Binary one-deletion followed by one-insertion composed model; exactly two codewords.
4099-term finite-state base proved by exact integer checker; no finite-only extrapolation.
